title: Gold Loan EMI Default: When Your Pledged Jewellery is at Risk
description: Missing a single gold loan EMI does not immediately lead to the auction of your pledged jewellery. Lenders must follow a specific recovery process, including .

faq.q: What happens if I miss just one gold loan EMI?
faq.a: If you miss one EMI, the lender will typically send reminders and a demand notice. Your gold is not immediately at risk of auction; there's a defined process with notice periods before any drastic action is taken.

faq.q: How much notice will I get before my gold is auctioned?
faq.a: As per RBI guidelines, lenders must provide a reasonable notice period, usually 30 days, before auctioning your gold. This final notice will specify the outstanding amount and the auction details.

faq.q: Can I stop the auction after receiving a final notice?
faq.a: Yes, you can stop the auction by paying the full outstanding loan amount, including principal, accrued interest, and any applicable charges, before the scheduled auction date.

faq.q: What if the auction price is more than my outstanding loan amount?
faq.a: If the auction proceeds exceed your total outstanding loan amount and all associated charges, the lender is legally obligated to return the surplus amount to you, the borrower.

faq.q: Are all gold loan lenders subject to the same RBI rules?
faq.a: Yes, all regulated entities, including banks and NBFCs offering gold loans, must adhere to the RBI's Fair Practices Code and guidelines regarding valuation, LTV, and recovery procedures.

faq.q: Can I get my gold back if it has already been auctioned?
faq.a: Once the gold has been legally auctioned and sold to a third party, it generally cannot be reclaimed. The only possibility is if the auction process was found to be fraudulent or not compliant with regulations, which would require legal intervention.

faq.q: Do I have to pay charges if I pre-close my gold loan?
faq.a: Pre-closure charges vary by lender. Some banks and NBFCs may levy a small pre-closure penalty, while others, especially for shorter-term loans, might not. Check your loan agreement for specific details.
